mainEvent.title: Tue 11/17 · Nvidia reports, its first quarter without Huang
mainEvent.body: Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close (results about 4:20p, call 5:00p) with interim CEO Colette Kress on the call. The Street expects non-GAAP EPS of about **$2.47–2.49** on revenue near **$109B** (guidance $108B ±2%) and wants a January-quarter outlook around $125B; options imply an 8–9% move. The stock fell another **4.1%** Monday to $156.14, about 10% below where it was before Jensen Huang resigned Thursday, and CNBC reports the board is not considering bringing him back despite the FT's report of a comeback campaign. It is a packed week: October retail sales Tuesday 8:30a, Fed minutes Wednesday 2:00p, Walmart Thursday before the open, and Anthropic's record IPO is expected to start trading Thursday.

stories.title: Nvidia reports Tuesday under a cloud.
stories.body: Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after Tuesday's close with interim CEO Colette Kress on the call. The stock fell 4.1% Monday to $156.14 and is down about 10% since Jensen Huang resigned Thursday (Kiplinger). The FT reported that Huang and allies are discussing a campaign to reinstate him, and Trump said he would not mind a return, but CNBC reports the board is not considering it and is focused on its investigation; Treasury Secretary Bessent has urged an outside CEO. Consensus is about $2.47–2.49 non-GAAP EPS on roughly $109B of revenue (guidance $108B ±2%). Polymarket gives about a 10% chance Huang rejoins Nvidia by Dec 31 and about 20% that a new permanent CEO is named by then; Arm's Rene Haas is now the favourite in the next-CEO market at about 28%.

stories.title: Tech rout tips the Nasdaq into a correction.
stories.body: The Nasdaq fell 2.49% to 24,509.76 Monday, more than 10% below its Oct 6 record close, as the S&P 500 lost 1.9%, the Dow 1.4% and the Russell 2000 1.7%. New interim US rules require licenses to re-export advanced AI chips to Brazil, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand ahead of a Trump–Xi meeting, which hit chips and AI infrastructure: Micron fell more than 6%, Dell about 7%, AMD 5.6%, and CoreWeave and Nebius about 6–7.5%. Intel lost 7% after a proposed shareholder class action alleging it concealed weak PC demand. Alphabet fell about 4% and Amazon 3.3%. The VIX jumped 18.7% to 22.91. Bank-app outages at JPMorgan, Bank of America and Wells Fargo added to the gloom, with no sign of a common cause.

stories.title: Anthropic's record IPO is set to debut Thursday.
stories.body: Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday night and start trading on Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT. It is selling 825 million shares at $70–78, up to about $64.4B, plus a $26B concurrent private placement (Nvidia and Google about $10B each), for about $90B in all (Bloomberg) at a valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion; the book is reported about six times oversubscribed. It would be the largest listing ever, and Bank of America's CEO says it is pushing some smaller listings into 2027. Polymarket prices a listing by Nov 19 at about 97%.

stories.title: Retail sales and Fed minutes test the hike case.
stories.body: Fed Chair Warsh used Monday's noon speech to walk through three illustrative AI scenarios for the economy and said nothing on rates, inflation or the market; Williams also skipped policy. Others were hawkish: Vice Chair Jefferson called inflation the most important consideration for further hikes, and Cleveland's Hammack said she prefers smaller steps, a sign she would not back 50bp. October retail sales land Tuesday at 8:30a (about +0.2% expected after +0.8%), and Wednesday's 2:00p minutes cover the Oct 27–28 meeting, where the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% with two members favoring a hike. CME FedWatch put a 25bp December hike at 93.7% Monday afternoon (Reuters); Kalshi and Polymarket are at about 88%.

stories.title: Retailers report into the holiday season.
stories.body: Home Depot (est. about $3.84–3.87 EPS) and Disney report Tuesday morning; Lowe's (about $2.86–2.89), TJX ($1.33) and Target (about $2.03–2.07) Wednesday; Walmart Thursday at 7:00a (about $0.63–0.64 on roughly $187B, guided $0.62–0.64), with Ross, Gap and Intuit after Thursday's close and BJ's Friday. Polymarket gives Disney about 82% to beat $1.69 and Home Depot about 47% to beat $3.95. Tuesday's retail sales set the tone.

stories.title: Oil drops 3% as Iran strike fears ease.
stories.body: WTI settled $2.84 lower at $85.72 and Brent $3.40 lower at $92.44 Monday (Newsquawk), after reports that the US is not considering imminent strikes on Iran and as recovering Middle East exports bolster the supply-surplus outlook (Reuters). That outweighed weekend Gulf tension, including Iranian attacks on Bahrain, and fresh Hormuz incidents: the IRGC says two tankers hit mines and UKMTO reported a tanker hit by a projectile.
